item.title: Florida Leaders Weigh In On November Constitutional Amendments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State officials are increasingly taking public positions on several constitutional amendments headed for the November ballot, according to reporting from Florida's government coverage this week. The amendments, which will require voter approval, are drawing attention from elected leaders across the state as campaigns ramp up ahead of Election Day.…
item.content:encoded:
State officials are increasingly taking public positions on several constitutional amendments headed for the November ballot, according to reporting from Florida's government coverage this week. The amendments, which will require voter approval, are drawing attention from elected leaders across the state as campaigns ramp up ahead of Election Day.

While details on specific amendments weren't fully available in initial reports, the pattern of officials staking out positions suggests the proposals may be controversial or significant enough to warrant public endorsement or opposition from state-level figures. Constitutional amendments in Florida require 60 percent voter approval to pass.

For Pensacola and Northwest Florida voters, these statewide ballot measures will appear alongside local races and issues in November. Residents interested in learning more about the amendments can expect increased media coverage and advocacy efforts in the coming weeks as groups on both sides of each proposal mobilize.

A Cantonment woman has been sentenced following a DUI arrest earlier this year, according to court records. An Escambia County Sheriff's Office deputy spotted her driving erratically on West Nine Mile Road and initiated a traffic stop that led to her arrest on charges including driving under the influence and drug possession.

The case was processed through Escambia County courts. Details about the specific sentence imposed were not immediately available, but the conviction adds to ongoing law enforcement efforts to address impaired driving in the county.

The arrest highlights continued patrols by ECSO deputies focused on traffic safety and enforcement of impaired driving laws across unincorporated areas of Escambia County.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's homecoming hopes took a hit Saturday night as visiting No. 14 Austin Peay pulled away in the second half to defeat the No. 17 Argonauts 38-16 at Pen Air Field.

Despite playing in front of home fans, UWF struggled early and couldn't recover from the deficit or overcome critical mistakes throughout the game. Austin Peay built momentum late in the contest to put the game firmly out of reach.

The loss marks a significant setback for the Argonauts in their Gulf South Conference schedule. UWF's next opportunity to bounce back comes with the start of their next conference matchup.

item.content:encoded:
Several Escambia County court facilities will be closed Monday, September 21 in observance of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Affected locations include the Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller offices at the M.C. Blanchard Judicial Building, the Theodore Bruno Building-Juvenile court facility, the Public Records Center, and the Billy G. Ward Courthouse in Century.

Residents and attorneys needing court services should plan accordingly and contact the courthouse for information about rescheduling any appointments or filings that may fall on the holiday.

item.title: Atmore Native Serves Aboard Nuclear Submarine USS Kentucky
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Seaman Tyanthony Dailey, a 2023 graduate of Escambia County High School, is now serving aboard the USS Kentucky, an Ohio-class ballistic-missile submarine that plays a critical role in America's nuclear deterrent strategy. Dailey, who grew up in Atmore, is among the sailors continuing the U.S. Navy's 126-year tradition of undersea operations. The…
item.content:encoded:
Seaman Tyanthony Dailey, a 2023 graduate of Escambia County High School, is now serving aboard the USS Kentucky, an Ohio-class ballistic-missile submarine that plays a critical role in America's nuclear deterrent strategy. Dailey, who grew up in Atmore, is among the sailors continuing the U.S. Navy's 126-year tradition of undersea operations.

The USS Kentucky is one of the Navy's most strategically important vessels, designed to patrol the world's oceans in relative secrecy as part of the nation's continuous at-sea deterrent. Submarine service is considered among the most demanding assignments in the military, requiring sailors to work in close quarters for extended periods while maintaining constant vigilance.

Dailey's assignment follows his recent graduation from high school in Escambia County, putting him among a select group of young service members who have chosen military careers immediately after finishing secondary education.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia can expect another hot summer day Sunday, with temperatures climbing near 92 degrees and heat index values potentially reaching 105, according to the National Weather Service forecast for the area.

There's a 50 percent chance of scattered showers and thunderstorms developing after 1 p.m., so afternoon plans may need flexibility. Winds will stay calm, picking up only slightly from the northwest around 5 mph.

If you're heading outside, plan morning activities before the heat and storm potential peak in the afternoon. Stay hydrated and be ready to move indoors if thunderstorms develop.

item.title: West Roberts Road Reopens After 3-Week Delay
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A section of West Roberts Road in North Escambia that shuttered in late August finally reopened Friday, though the project remains behind schedule. The closure began August 29, with crews initially targeting a Labor Day weekend reopening. Instead, commuters waited nearly three weeks before the road became passable again last Friday, September 18.…
item.content:encoded:
A section of West Roberts Road in North Escambia that shuttered in late August finally reopened Friday, though the project remains behind schedule. The closure began August 29, with crews initially targeting a Labor Day weekend reopening. Instead, commuters waited nearly three weeks before the road became passable again last Friday, September 18.

The delay marks another chapter in what locals have come to know as the West Roberts Road construction saga — a project that has tested the patience of North Escambia residents navigating the corridor. Officials haven't yet clarified whether additional closures are planned, leaving some uncertainty about what comes next for the troubled thoroughfare.

The reopening provides temporary relief for drivers in the area, though the headline in the project's history — "maybe not for long" — suggests more work remains. Residents should stay alert for future announcements about any continued construction activity on West Roberts Road.

item.content:encoded: The Summerdale town council voted 4-2 Saturday to bring Police Chief Mike Guall back to work following his placement on administrative leave, according to WKRG News 5. The reinstatement means Guall will resume his duties with the Summerdale Police Department after the period away from the position.

item.content:encoded:
The eighth annual Joy of Life charity golf tournament will tee off October 16 in Fairhope, with proceeds going to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. Registration opens at 8 a.m., followed by a shotgun start at 9 a.m., according to WKRG News 5.

The tournament has become an established fixture in the region's charity golf calendar, raising funds for the Memphis-based pediatric cancer research and treatment center. St. Jude never charges families for treatment, travel, housing or food—services that rely heavily on community fundraising efforts like this one.

More details about entry fees, sponsorship opportunities, and the Fairhope course location are available through the Joy of Life website.

item.content:encoded:
If you're planning your weekend around college football, here's what's on the schedule for Saturday. A slate of matchups kicks off in the morning and early afternoon, with several ranked teams in action across major networks.

Coastal Carolina faces Delaware at 10:30 a.m. on CBSSN to get things started. An hour later, the real heavyweights take the field: No. 2 Georgia travels to Arkansas on ABC, No. 6 Ohio State hosts Kent State on FOX, and No. 14 Penn State welcomes Buffalo. All three of those matchups are set for 11 a.m. Central time.

According to North Escambia, that's the early window for Saturday's college action. Whether you're rooting for a ranked powerhouse or tuning in for the lower-profile FCS matchups, most of the games fall into that morning-to-early-afternoon window, so plan your Saturday accordingly.

item.title: Hot Weekend Ahead for Pensacola Area; Storms Possible Sunday
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Saturday looks like a textbook summer day — mostly sunny skies with a high near 94 degrees and light north winds that'll die off through the afternoon. Overnight, conditions will stay pleasant…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola area is in for a scorcher this weekend, with temperatures climbing into the low-to-mid 90s and heat index values pushing toward 105 degrees.

Saturday looks like a textbook summer day — mostly sunny skies with a high near 94 degrees and light north winds that'll die off through the afternoon. Overnight, conditions will stay pleasant with partly cloudy skies and lows around 73 degrees.

Sunday is when things get a bit more interesting. There's a 50 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 1 p.m., though the day will start mostly sunny. Highs will be similar to Saturday, near 92 degrees, but the heat index could still climb to around 105 degrees when you factor in humidity.

If you're planning outdoor activities, Saturday morning or early afternoon looks like your best bet before Sunday's potential storm system moves in.

item.content:encoded:
The Molino Community Center and Molino Library will shut down for the next week while crews restore the building's original flooring. The work is expected to wrap up by Saturday, September 26, according to facility officials.

While the library itself will be inaccessible during the closure, patrons can still return books using the external book drop located outside the building. The community center's other services and programs will also be unavailable during this period.

Residents in north Escambia County who need library services during the closure can visit other branches in the county system, or wait until the restoration is complete and the Molino location reopens.

item.title: UWF partners with Home Base Florida to expand veteran wellness services
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida has launched a new partnership with Home Base Florida to bring the Warrior Health and Fitness program to its Pensacola campus, expanding access to wellness resources for veterans, active-duty service members, and military families across Northwest Florida. According to WKRG News 5, the collaboration aims to address…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida has launched a new partnership with Home Base Florida to bring the Warrior Health and Fitness program to its Pensacola campus, expanding access to wellness resources for veterans, active-duty service members, and military families across Northwest Florida.

According to WKRG News 5, the collaboration aims to address health and fitness needs specific to the military community in the region. The program will operate through UWF's campus, making it more accessible to eligible participants in Escambia County and surrounding areas.

Home Base Florida specializes in veteran support and wellness initiatives, while UWF brings institutional resources and community connections. The partnership underscores the university's commitment to serving the large military population in the Pensacola area, which includes NAS Pensacola and numerous other defense installations.

Details about program enrollment, specific services offered, and launch timing were not immediately available. Interested veterans, service members, or family members should contact UWF directly for more information about accessing the Warrior Health and Fitness program.
